args.evidence: raw.orders has 15000 rows distinct order_key; stg_orders also 15000 distinct; fct_order_items has 60175 rows (multiple items per order). fct_orders also 60175 rows but only 15000 distinct order_key, causing duplicate key check failure. The fct_orders model joins items aggregated by order_key and line_number, resulting in one row per line item. Removing line_number from GROUP BY will produce one row per order, fixing duplicates.

args.explanation: The duplicate key failure was caused by the items CTE grouping by both order_key and line_number, which produced one row per line item. By grouping only on order_key, we aggregate all items per order, ensuring a single row per order_key in fct_orders. This resolves the unique_fct_orders_order_key check while preserving all existing columns and types.
